fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Fall Into the Osirian Underworld", "body": "Chance opened by calling episode four the fall and the beginning of the underworld cycle, a major theme in Egyptian mythology, in which the dying and resurrecting Osiris was embodied by initiates and pharaohs. The hosts read the opening hanged man ritual, with its twisting camera, as Osiris entering the underworld, and Gabe tied the polar imagery, the maze and the path to Mario Garza's work on the pole star. One of the hosts argued the show inverted Egyptian ideas by treating statues as literal gods instead of symbolic access points."}, {"title": "Scorpio, Betrayal and the Far Strider", "body": "The hosts followed a Scorpio thread through the episode. Chance argued that Layla's Scorpio sign, the kiss of betrayal and the fall that follows it formed the main beats, and that Layla played both Isis and Nephthys. Gabe argued she acted as Hecate, the goddess of two torches, luring the pursuers with one flare and striking from behind with the second. One of the hosts added that her long leaps across gaps fulfilled the Hecate title of far strider, and that the flare worked as a stand in for the missing Osirian phallus."}, {"title": "Scarab, Scapegoat and Masonic Third Degree", "body": "The hosts read the scarab on its mound as a sign of rebirth, and one of them read a passage from the book July's End on the sacred scarab, its twenty eight day cycle and the shift from scarab to crab. The goat in the canyon became a Yom Kippur scapegoat, and one host linked the scarab to the root of that ritual. Another host described the Masonic third degree tracing boards. Gabe offered a theory that the dry river bed matched the Mississippi River, which he linked to Old Testament geography and the devil card."}, {"title": "Heka, Canopic Jars and the Word Can", "body": "At the hidden chamber the hosts took up Heka as both magic and medicine, and read the cannibal pharaoh passage from the Pyramid Texts. One host played with the syllable can across canopic, canopy, cane and cannabis, while another argued that the snake skin grafted onto an arm pointed to a grafted bloodline. Gabe noticed that the cups, the jars and the snake skin seen from the rafters resembled the dippers and Draco around the pole star, which he said marked the exit. The zombie priest pulling entrails drew an Ophiuchus comparison."}, {"title": "Dream Asylum, Jung and the Tertium Quid", "body": "In the white asylum the hosts treated the bingo calls as a cipher, and one host decoded the numbers into letters that spelled a vote. They read the scene as a black mass and as a dream whose edges come apart. Harrow, dressed as Carl Jung, said the world is lived inside the psyche, and one host called Jung a two sided sword that can be used for or against us. The hosts tied taking inventory of feelings to organs kept in canopic jars, and one host explained the red third sarcophagus as the tertium quid, a third self linked to the placenta, before Taweret appeared."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In our continuing quest to analyze the occult and mythological significance of symbolism in the Moon Knight series, we press onward to explore episode 4, "The Tomb." Major themes include the death and resurrection of the Sun-King, the dismemberment of Osiris, exposing the poor portrayal of ancient Egyptian ideas, and the ever-present broken mirror MK Ultra schizoid soul-division.
